newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens to divest two units by end of 97.
newsitem.headline: Siemens to divest two units by end of 97.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG said on Thursday it expected sales of its dental technology and defence electronics businesses to go through by the end of this year.
Siemens was talking to several potential buyers for each unit, but declined to name those companies.
Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), a unit of car maker Daimler-Benz AG said earlier this week at the Paris air show that it had submitted a bid for the defence group.
Industry executives at the same show said French defence group Thomson-CSF was bidding for the Siemens unit as well.
"We are talking to several potential buyers, but we are not commenting on the specific companies," Siemens spokesman Thomas Weber said when asked about the defence sale.
He also declined to comment on whether German buyers would have an edge over companies based in other countries.
Dasa chief executive Manfred Bischoff said his company sought the Siemens group to accelerate a consolidation of German defence companies.
Siemens has retained investment bank Morgan Stanley to help find a buyer for the defence unit.

In the six-month period to March 31, Siemens' defence business, which includes Siemens-Plessey in Britain, saw sales fall 16 percent to 600 million marks ($346.6 million) while orders fell 14 percent to 600 million marks.
A spokesman for Siemens medical technology group said several companies were interested in its 900 million mark dental business and that the sale was expected to be completed this year.
Siemens has said it planned to sell or put into joint ventures units with a combined business volume of about 5.5 billion marks over the next 12 to 18 months.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.731 German Marks)
